newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end down 1/2 to 3/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end down 1/2 to 3/4.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds declined 1/2 to 3/4 of a point Thursday, as U.S. Treasuries nursed nearly a full point's worth of data-induced wounds heading into Friday's February producer price index report.
"We've been rich to Treasuries," one trader said. "And obviously, when Treasuries go down, we get dragged down with it."
The municipal market has also seen a fair amount of new issues this week and last, the trader said.

"The the mutual funds, as you know,...have no money," the trader said. "And the insurance companies, they've been buying a little bit, they've been nibbling, but certainly not enough to absorb all the bonds around. So we went down a solid 05 (five basis points) today."
The trader also cited "a fairly good amount" of bid wanteds circulating on Thursday. He estimated the lists' par value at $250 million to $300 million.
"That's not a big day any more," the trader said.

A municipal analyst said the overall market was down 1/2 to 3/4 of a point, and more in spots. High-grade issues worsened by about five basis points, while dollar bonds ended down 5/8 to 3/4 of a point. The analyst described secondary activity as "light," though he also cited lists.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 30/32 at 95-26/32 to yield 6.96 percent amid heightened expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed down 31/32 at 112-15/32. The June T-bond contract closed down 1-5/32 at 108-16/32. The MOB spread was 127 ticks.

Early in the session, the Commerce Department said retail sales rose 0.8 percent in February, compared to a large upward revision for January to a 1.5 percent rise. Excluding autos, sales rose 0.5 percent last month.

Economists polled by Reuters expected February sales to rise 0.6 percent overall and 0.7 percent excluding autos. Also Thursday, the Labor Department said initial jobless claims for the week ended March 8 fell to 307,000 from 312,000 in the prior week.

Looking ahead to Friday's numbers, economists polled by Reuters expect February PPI to show a 0.1 percent decline overall, and a 0.1 percent gain in the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices.
Also Friday, the market is scheduled to receive January business inventories data as well as February figures on industrial production and capacity utilization.

In new issues, PaineWebber Inc won $30 million of Jersey City, N.J., school bonds at a net interest cost of 5.50 percent, and $16.8 million of Jersey City water bonds with a net interest cost of 5.52 percent.
